Q: Simulate Location including movement in Xcode 4.2 / iOS5 A:

Speed can be controlled by modifying the time between each set of latitude and longitude pairs. Xcode calculates speed from the distance between consecutive waypoints divided by the time gap between their time tags. You can increase or decrease the time then moreless to control the speed. Late to the party but hope this helps

Q: In Power Automate Desktop with Power Fx enabled, how do I get files while filtering them by a wildcard? A:

The File Filter expects text, and =FilePrefix* is not any kind of text expression. =FilePrefix & "*" is a text expression, but a File Filter should have a file type extension, so maybe something like =FilePrefix & "*.jpg" is what you want. It would help so much if you told us what FilePrefix is, and what files you want to filter.

Q: Is it possible to print a number formatted with thousand separator in Rust? A:

The simplest way to format a number with thousands separator without Locale is to use the thousands crate.

use thousands::Separable;

println!("{}", 10_000_000.separate_with_commas());
a one-liner

using only the Rust std library

let num = 10_000_000.to_string()
    .as_bytes()
    .rchunks(3)
    .rev()
    .map(std::str::from_utf8)
    .collect::<Result<Vec<&str>, _>>()
    .unwrap()
    .join(",");  // separator

Playground contains an enhanced solution that also formats negative numbers

Q: Containers written as HOCs? (in the Container/Presentational pattern) A:

but then every time I look at a container, at the end it calls one specific presentation, which for me, seems to be limiting the reusability of the container.

This is because the presentation components are typically "generic" or "generalized" UI components and the container components fit very specific use cases and feed specific data to the presentation layer.

I'm a little confused why I can't find anything that addresses this issue. It seems like an HOC should be perfect to decouple the two entirely so they're both fully reusable with separate containers / presentations.

You probably should take a read of Dan Abramov's (a React core maintainer and one of the creators of Redux, and IIRC is the originator or at least an early champion of the pattern) article about the container/presentation pattern. SPOILER: he no longer recommends it as React hooks largely solve the problem the container/presentation pattern addressed.

FWIW, Higher Order Components are also largely unnecessary now because of React hooks.

Because of this is possibly why you are unable to find much of anything that addresses using them specifically, React hooks have been around since 2019 afterall.

This all said though, sure, HOCs still have a place in the React ecosystem with regards to code-reusability.

TL;DR: The Container & Presentation Component pattern and Higher Order Component pattern solve different problems. They can be used together.
